narrative.overview:
biring is a book kept in the hand: one mint pen, a graphite cover, plain paper. The system never decorates the ledger. It makes the numbers legible, the next action obvious, and the state of a row unmistakable at a glance. Mint is the pen. Graphite is the cover. Hairlines are the ruled paper.

Structure follows Material's grammar — screen context at the top, destinations in a bottom bar, one floating add action, a centred dialog for decisions — but the surfaces are quieter than stock Material: no raised cards, no tonal confetti, no shadow ladder. Depth is one pixel of border and one step of tone. Type does the rest: Public Sans at four weights, sentence case, with uppercase used only as a whisper.

This is an Operate surface, used one-thumbed in shops and kitchens. Every screen is a single column; forms pin their action at the bottom, and no screen asks the visitor to learn a new control. Expression lives in the cover: the month dashboard and Summary are always graphite, always dark, their totals in bold Chalk and their categories as mint bars — then the page turns to paper below.
keyCharacteristics: Mint is the only accent; red is reserved for irreversible acts and errors.
Flat by default: 1px hairlines and tonal steps instead of shadows.
The dashboard and Summary wear a graphite cover in both light and dark themes.
Public Sans carries hierarchy through four family files, never through fontWeight.
Pills for actions, 16px panels for content, 24px only where a surface meets a screen edge.
At most one filled pill per screen, pinned above the bottom bar or safe area.

rules.name: The One Accent Rule
rules.body: Mint is the only brand hue. It marks action, selection, and progress; destructive red appears only on irreversible actions and errors. Roughly a tenth of any screen carries colour — the rest is paper.

rules.name: The Fixed Graphite Rule
rules.body: The graphite family does not flip with the theme. Only page, card, text, and hairline swap. A graphite surface is graphite in both schemes.

rules.name: The On-Mint Rule
rules.body: Text and icons on a mint fill are always Deep Pine — never white, never graphite.

rules.name: The Face-Not-Weight Rule
rules.body: In React Native, weight is a family: font-sans, font-sans-medium, font-sans-semibold, font-sans-bold. A fontWeight class or style prop silently falls back to system Roboto.

rules.name: The One Uppercase Rule
rules.body: Only eyebrows and month headers are uppercase. Titles, labels, buttons, and body copy stay sentence case.

rules.name: The Dark Cover Rule
rules.body: The dashboard and Summary are graphite in both themes; the sheet below is the themed page. Totals live on the cover, detail on the page.

rules.name: The One Column Rule
rules.body: Never introduce a grid, sidebar, or multi-column card layout. The phone in one hand is the whole canvas.

rules.name: The Hairline Rule
rules.body: Depth is 1px of border plus one step of tone. If a new surface must lift, it is either the FAB or a dialog with a scrim — nothing else casts a shadow.

rules.name: The Pill-and-Panel Rule
rules.body: Pills for things you press, 16px panels for things that hold content, 24px only where a surface meets the screen edge. Never give a card a pill radius or a button a panel radius.

dos: Do start every screen with a safe area (top, plus bottom on forms) and bg-canvas dark:bg-graphite; the dashboard and Summary are the always-graphite screens.
Do pair every light token with its dark partner: canvas/graphite, surface/graphite-surface, edge/graphite-border, graphite/on-graphite, muted/silver, placeholder/placeholder-dark.
Do choose weight with family classes (font-sans-semibold) and keep body copy at 16–18px.
Do use 24px gutters, 16px card padding, 8px between a label and its field, and 20–24px between blocks.
Do make the primary action a single full-width filled pill pinned at the bottom of forms.
Do keep headline totals in Bold; let long category amounts shrink with adjustsFontSizeToFit rather than wrap.
Do explain state in plain words under the control ("Saves on this device and syncs when you're online.") in Slate or Ash, never by colour or icon alone.
Do use 1px hairlines and the tonal pairs for structure; keep the FAB the only elevated object.
Do give icon-only controls at least 40px and add 8px hitSlop where the icon is the only target; aim for 48dp on new controls.
Do keep sentence case everywhere except eyebrows and month headers.
Do disable offline-blocked actions instead of hiding them, and say why: "Creating, joining, and signing out need a connection."
donts: Don't add a second accent. There is no secondary brand colour, no gradient, and no tinted card wash except Mint Wash behind mint content.
Don't put shadows on cards, dialogs, or fields, and don't stack elevation on the tab bar.
Don't use Void Red for anything but void, archive, leave, and errors; never as the primary action of a normal flow.
Don't put white or Chalk text on mint; on-mint is always Deep Pine.
Don't use 16px panel radii on the dashboard sheet (24px) or pill radii on cards.
Don't uppercase body copy, labels, or buttons.
Don't set fontSize or fontWeight inline; use the type classes so the four family files stay authoritative.
Don't port iOS controls or a Cupertino look: switches, action sheets, and bottom drawers are not part of this system. Decisions use the centred dialog.
Don't add a native header; the app bar is in-page so the cover can stay edge-to-edge.
Don't reuse the theme toggle's track and sun/moon colours (#2b3244, #bfdcff, #475569, #f59e0b) anywhere else.
